ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 3, a wooden block P of mass m slides on a long wooden board ab of mass M, and the long wooden board is placed on the horizontal ground and remains at rest throughout. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the long wooden board ab and the ground is $\mu_{1}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the wooden block P and the long wooden board ab is $\mu_{2}$, find the magnitude of the friction force exerted by the ground on the long wooden board ab.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, a long wooden board is placed horizontally on the ground indicated by diagonal lines, the left end of the wooden board is labeled a, and the right end is labeled b; the wooden block P is placed above the long wooden board, and above the wooden block there is a velocity arrow v pointing to the right, indicating that P slides to the right relative to the board; the problem statement explains that the long wooden board is always at rest. Then reason: relative sliding occurs between the wooden block P and the long wooden board; P slides to the right relative to the board, so the sliding friction force exerted by the long wooden board on P is to the left, with magnitude f=μ2N. In the vertical direction, P is in balance under the support force and gravity, so N=mg, so the magnitude of the friction force exerted by the long wooden board on P is μ2mg. According to Newton's third law, the friction force exerted by P on the long wooden board is to the right, with the same magnitude μ2mg. The long wooden board remains at rest throughout, and the resultant force in the horizontal direction is zero, so the friction force exerted by the ground on the long wooden board must be to the left and equal in magnitude to the friction force exerted by P on the wooden board. Therefore, the magnitude of the friction force exerted by the ground on the long wooden board ab is μ2mg.
